documentation.summary: Control how elements participate in document flow, how they are positioned, and how overflowing or replaced content is handled.
documentation.guidance: Choose display first, add position only when the element must leave or track normal flow, then use logical inset utilities when the interface must work in both LTR and RTL directions.
concepts: Display utilities determine the formatting context before flex or grid alignment is applied.
Sticky positioning needs a scroll container and at least one inset such as co-top-0.
Logical inset-s/inset-e and inset-bs/inset-be utilities follow inline and block writing directions; start/end remain compatibility aliases.
Aspect ratios accept named tokens, numeric fractions, custom properties, and arbitrary values.
Page and column break utilities compose with print and responsive variants.
caveats: Multi-column count, gap, and rule styling are tracked in the separate Tables and columns family.
Negative values are intentionally limited to inset, positional offsets, and z-index.

documentation.summary: Build one- and two-dimensional layouts with flex direction, wrapping, grid tracks, spans, automatic placement, and alignment utilities.
documentation.guidance: Use flex for content distributed along one primary axis and grid when rows and columns must coordinate. Apply gap on the container and span/start/end utilities on children.
concepts: co-flex and co-grid only establish layout mode; direction and track definitions remain explicit.
Numeric grid tracks use repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr)) to prevent content overflow.
Subgrid adopts tracks from the parent grid instead of creating an independent track list.
Safe alignment falls back toward the start edge when centered or end-aligned content would overflow.
Grid lines and order accept canonical negative syntax before the co- prefix.
caveats: Masonry is intentionally excluded until interoperable browser support is stable.
Named grid lines use arbitrary values or CSS custom properties because names belong to the application schema.

documentation.summary: Apply physical and logical padding, margin, gaps, sibling spacing, scroll margin, and scroll padding from the shared spacing scale.
documentation.guidance: Prefer gap for flex and grid children, space utilities for ordinary sibling flow, and logical ps/pe/pbs/pbe or ms/me/mbs/mbe utilities when direction-aware writing modes are required.
concepts: Numeric values multiply --co-space-unit, which defaults to 0.25rem.
Fractions resolve to percentages and px resolves to one CSS pixel.
Logical start/end utilities adapt to direction while block-start/block-end adapt to writing mode.
Sibling space utilities target every direct child except the last and include explicit reverse-axis controls.
Scroll spacing mirrors physical and logical padding/margin edges.
caveats: Negative values are intentionally valid for margin, scroll margin, and sibling spacing—not padding, gap, or scroll padding.
Position offsets are documented in Layout even though they share the same value resolver.
Dynamically concatenated spacing classes cannot be detected by the scanner.

documentation.summary: Set physical or logical dimensions, minimum and maximum constraints, and paired width/height with spacing, container, viewport, intrinsic, custom-property, or arbitrary values.
documentation.guidance: Use size when width and height share a value, inline/block when components must respect writing mode, and min/max constraints when content or viewport changes must not break the component.
concepts: Fraction utilities produce percentages such as co-w-1/2 → 50%.
Named 3xs through 7xl container tokens provide reusable inline dimensions.
screen, svh/svw, lvh/lvw, and dvh/dvw cover viewport behavior while lh follows the current line height.
min, max, fit, and none map to intrinsic or unconstrained sizing keywords.
CSS custom properties use parenthesized shorthand such as co-inline-(--panel-size).
caveats: Sizing utilities intentionally reject negative values.
Flex basis belongs to the Flexbox and grid family.
Logical sizes depend on the element's writing mode, which is controlled separately.

documentation.summary: Control font families, variable-font width and features, type scale, weight, leading, tracking, numeric glyphs, lists, alignment, decoration, wrapping, indentation, tab width, and generated content.
documentation.guidance: Start with the CSS-first font and text tokens, use a font-size/line-height modifier when the pair belongs together, and reserve arbitrary values for type decisions that should not become reusable design tokens.
concepts: Font-size tokens may carry default line-height, letter-spacing, and font-weight metadata, while slash modifiers such as co-text-sm/6 override only line height.
Font-family tokens may carry feature and variation defaults; standalone font-features utilities provide explicit OpenType control.
Font stretch accepts named widths, percentages, CSS custom properties, and arbitrary values.
Line clamp combines overflow, display, box orientation, and clamp declarations.
Text colors and decoration colors share the theme color namespace.
Overflow wrapping distinguishes break-word from anywhere so intrinsic flex sizing can be handled intentionally.
Generated content composes with before/after variants and preserves scanner-visible literal values.
caveats: Font files and @font-face declarations remain authored CSS assets rather than generated utilities.
OpenType and variable-font results depend on glyph support in the selected font.
Only tracking and indentation accept the canonical negative modifier; content utilities are normally paired with before or after variants.

documentation.summary: Apply theme, inherited, current, transparent, or arbitrary colors; compose linear, radial, and conic gradients; and control every background image layer setting.
documentation.guidance: Prefer theme colors and named background-image tokens, compose gradients from an explicit direction plus from/via/to stops, and use typed arbitrary values when image, color, position, or size syntax could be ambiguous.
concepts: Theme colors compile through --co-color-* variables and named images through --co-background-image-* variables.
Slash opacity uses color-mix in OKLab instead of duplicating palette entries.
Linear, radial, and conic gradients share composable from/via/to colors and percentage positions.
Gradient interpolation modifiers support sRGB, HSL, OKLab, OKLCH, and OKLCH hue-path controls.
Position and size accept named values, CSS custom-property shorthand, and safe arbitrary values.
caveats: Wide-gamut palette design and Display-P3 authoring are tracked separately by the Modern color capability.
Background images referenced by URL remain application assets and are not bundled by the compiler.

documentation.summary: Define physical and logical border widths and colors, styles, corner radii, accessible outlines, outward and inset rings, legacy ring offsets, and complete dividers between children.
documentation.guidance: Use borders for element geometry, outlines for keyboard focus without layout movement, rings for composable focus treatment, and divide utilities only when sibling separators belong to the parent layout.
concepts: Physical and logical border axes accept numeric pixels, typed custom properties, and safe arbitrary lengths.
Every border edge accepts theme, inherited, current, transparent, arbitrary, and slash-opacity colors.
Radius tokens and custom values apply to complete boxes, physical sides, logical sides, and individual corners.
Outward and inset rings compose with each other and ordinary shadows through shared custom properties.
Divide width, reverse direction, color, and style target every direct child except the last.
caveats: The ring-offset utilities remain as a compatibility extension even though current Tailwind-style rings no longer require an offset layer.
Logical corners and edges follow writing mode and direction, so visual placement changes intentionally in RTL or vertical text.

documentation.summary: Control elevation, text shadows, opacity, blending, composable filters, backdrop filters, and CSS or SVG masks.
documentation.guidance: Use named shadow and blur tokens for repeatable visual depth, combine filter utilities freely, and use masks only when clipping cannot express the intended alpha or luminance shape.
concepts: Box shadows remain composable with outward and inset rings through shared shadow layers.
Shadow, text-shadow, and drop-shadow colors use dedicated custom properties so theme colors and opacity modifiers can recolor named geometry.
Filter and backdrop-filter functions are stored in independent custom properties, allowing blur, brightness, contrast, hue rotation, and other functions to compose regardless of class order.
Mask utilities cover image sources, alpha or luminance mode, geometry boxes, positioning, repetition, sizing, compositing, SVG mask type, and linear fade helpers.
Opacity values are expressed as percentages in class names and decimals in CSS.
caveats: Opacity affects the element and all descendants as a composited group.
Backdrop filters only become visible when content exists behind a translucent element.
Arbitrary mask and filter values must remain literal and are rejected when declaration-breaking characters are detected.

documentation.summary: Control semantic table display, layout algorithms, collapsed or separated borders, cell spacing, captions, and multi-column content flow.
documentation.guidance: Use table-auto when content should influence column widths, table-fixed for predictable tracks, and multi-column flow for editorial content rather than application grids.
concepts: Table display utilities cover table, row, cell, caption, column, and header/footer/body grouping roles.
Border spacing supports shared, horizontal, and vertical values and only applies when borders are separated.
Column count utilities accept numbers while container-size tokens such as co-columns-sm define an ideal column width.
Multi-column gaps reuse gap utilities and page or column break controls reuse the complete Layout family.
Column fill, spanning, and rule width/color/style provide explicit editorial flow controls beyond the baseline table utilities.
caveats: Responsive table overflow still requires an explicit wrapper because table layout does not create a scroll container.
Multi-column layout follows source order vertically before continuing horizontally, so it is unsuitable for data grids or reading orders that must remain row-based.
Column rules occupy the gap without changing its calculated width.

documentation.summary: Translate, rotate, scale, skew, and change transform origin using independent modern CSS transform properties where possible.
documentation.guidance: Apply transform utilities to the element being moved, keep layout spacing separate, and use negative modifiers for reverse translation or rotation.
concepts: Translate values reuse the spacing and fraction scales.
Rotation and skew numeric values are interpreted as degrees.
Transform origin accepts named positions or arbitrary values.
caveats: 3D translate/rotate, transform-style, perspective, and perspective-origin remain planned.
Skew currently uses the transform shorthand and should not be mixed carelessly with other shorthand transforms.

documentation.summary: Choose transition properties, duration, delay, and easing without adding a browser runtime.
documentation.guidance: Transition only properties that need animation, respect reduced-motion variants, and keep interaction durations short and consistent.
concepts: The default transition covers common visual properties.
Duration and delay numeric values are interpreted as milliseconds.
motion-safe and motion-reduce variants can wrap transition utilities.
caveats: Animation names and built-in keyframes are not implemented.
Starting-style and discrete transition helpers remain planned.

documentation.summary: Set SVG fill and stroke colors from theme tokens, currentColor, or arbitrary values.
documentation.guidance: Use currentColor when an icon should inherit surrounding text color and theme colors when fill or stroke needs independent semantic meaning.
concepts: Fill and stroke use the shared color resolver.
Stroke width accepts 0, 1, 2, numeric arbitrary values, and CSS lengths.
State and responsive variants compose with SVG utilities.
caveats: Use arbitrary properties for SVG presentation attributes outside fill, stroke color, and stroke width.
SVG presentation attributes may compete with generated CSS specificity.

documentation.summary: Visually hide content while keeping it available to assistive technology, then restore it under focus or another variant.
documentation.guidance: Use co-sr-only for descriptive labels and focus:co-not-sr-only for skip links that should appear during keyboard navigation.
concepts: Screen-reader-only content remains in the accessibility tree.
Forced-color adjustment controls whether user-agent high-contrast colors override an element.
Color-scheme utilities declare supported light and dark browser UI schemes.
caveats: Do not use sr-only to hide interactive content that must remain unreachable.
Use forced-color-adjust-none only when preserving authored colors is essential for meaning.

documentation.summary: Control cursors, pointer events, text selection, resize handles, appearance, scroll snapping, touch gestures, and change hints.
documentation.guidance: Use interaction utilities to reflect real behavior, not only visual intent, and preserve keyboard and assistive-technology access.
concepts: Scroll snap needs a snap type on the container and snap alignment on children.
Touch action tells the browser which gestures the application handles.
will-change should be temporary and used sparingly.
caveats: Additional cursor keywords and touch combinations remain.
pointer-events-none does not automatically remove descendants from keyboard navigation.

documentation.summary: Emit a validated CSS property/value pair when no first-class utility represents a one-off requirement.
documentation.guidance: Use arbitrary properties as an escape hatch, keep them literal for scanning, and promote repeated values into theme tokens or registered utilities later.
concepts: Syntax is co-[property:value].
Unescaped underscores inside arbitrary values become spaces while \_ remains an underscore.
Type hints disambiguate color, length, image, position, font family, and font weight values.
Property names and declaration values are validated before CSS is emitted.
caveats: User-provided arbitrary values are emitted as CSS and should come from trusted source code, not runtime input.
Repeated arbitrary values should be promoted to theme tokens for consistency.
